analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES – TSMC Terafab talks; DSY read from Schneider; BT acquires TalkTalk; DT AI CMD; AI Credit; Q3 semis preview
key_insights: TSMC hit an all-time high after Elon Musk confirmed preliminary talks on a TSMC role in Terafab's Texas chip project. Initial investment is US$16.8bn and total planned spending is US$55-119bn. A partnership could reduce execution risk but complicate Intel's role. No agreement has been reached.
TSMC reports on 15 October, with focus on capex, CoWoS, Texas and pricing. ASML reports the day before.

GS semis Q3 preview (Jim) is constructive after the SOX fell 11% over two months. Expectations are now more achievable and upside is likely across most sub-sectors. Preferred: SemiCap, compute, select analog, memory/storage. Preferred into earnings: AMAT, STX, MCHP. Relatively less attractive: QCOM, KLAC, WDC.

SIA data: August IC shipments excluding memory rose about 2% m/m, ahead of seasonal norms. Total semiconductor shipments run about 10% above long-term demand trend on a 3-month moving average, up from 7% in July. Analog shipments are also about 10% above trend. Goldman is most positive on Microchip, NXP and Analog Devices, which under-shipped the most in the downturn.

Schneider Electric agreed an all-cash acquisition of PTC at $205/share. Equity value is about $22.6B and EV about $23.7B, a premium of about 42%. GS sees it as raising the bar for Dassault Systemes (DSY) without being existential. DSY keeps differentiation in multi-physics simulation and complex long-cycle verticals.

DSY is a consensus short, so near-term squeeze risk exists after the Schneider/PTC M&A validation of the space. Medium-term, DSY must accelerate its data/AI layer or risk share shifts. A takeover of DSY is not simple because the Dassault family controls about 39.9-40.5%.

BT confirmed the acquisition of TalkTalk and PlatformX out of administration on a debt-free basis. Estimated FY27 cash impact is about £400m, including a c£60m trading loss and non-receipt of c£100m owed to Openreach. BT reiterated underlying FY27 and multi-year guidance and expects the deal to become value accretive. Regulatory review and execution risk remain.

Deutsche Telekom's AI investor event targets about €800m of AI-related revenue from non-US enterprise customers by 2030 and about €2.5bn of indirect cost savings versus 2023. Guidance and medium-term targets were confirmed.

Q3 earnings (Ben Snider): consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y, with AI beneficiaries accounting for more than half. Hyperscaler capex is up 116%. Median stock EPS growth slows from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3. Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth is expected to accelerate to 55% in Q3.

US long/short net leverage fell for a third consecutive week to 46.4%, the lowest since April 2025 and in the 2nd percentile of the 5-year range. Europe saw its largest percentage net buying in over five years.

AI credit (Adam Crook): hyperscaler debt issuance is estimated at about $250bn in 2026 (under $20bn in 2024) and $420bn in 2027. Hyperscalers are about 40% of more than $575bn of global AI-related debt issuance this year. Issuance is shifting to shorter maturities. GS rates strategists say the supply reduces appetite for duration and raises the chance that long-term yields overshoot fair value.

OpenAI safety employee David Robinson resigned, saying the company prioritises rapid iterative deployment over rigorous safeguards. OpenAI said it is strengthening security, third-party testing and real-time monitoring.

Memory: NVDA may secure only about 60% of its 2027 LPDDR5X needs, which could halve Vera Rubin SOCAMM capacity. Tight supply could sustain PC and smartphone price pressure through 1H27, with memory potentially near 40% of smartphone BOM costs (Digitimes).

The US may phase in restrictions on Chinese optical modules starting at 3.2T, possibly from October. Imports could stay permitted if at least 65% of BOM value is from US companies. Current 800G and 1.6T products would reportedly be outside the initial scope.
Quanta reportedly suspended HP notebook production for one week in September to negotiate higher prices. Servers were over 80% of Quanta's 2Q26 revenue.

Marvell sees 3-4+ supporting custom-chip opportunities per XPU, and inference-driven KV-cache demand is up roughly 10x in nine months. Some sell-side forecasts put ASIC/XPU shipment share at 54% in 2027 and 55% in 2028. AVGO and Marvell hold about 90% of the custom AI ASIC market.

AWS plans to invest more than $1bn over five years in US communities hosting its data centres and pledges to be water positive by 2030. A Gallup survey found 71% of Americans oppose a local AI data centre.
Fiserv Small Business Index: September spending growth was 2.2% SA versus 1.2% in August. Transaction growth was -2.0% y/y and average ticket grew 4.3% y/y.

UK CMA found the nexfibre/Netomnia deal could substantially reduce wholesale broadband competition. GS views this as incrementally negative for VMO2 (TEF/LBTYA) and BT, and sees altnet consolidation as necessary for fixed market repair.

AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are forming a joint venture to pool spectrum and technical standards for direct-to-device satellite coverage, a response to Starlink. There is no service date or venture name yet.

European agencies: media growth at large holdcos has accelerated to about 6% in 2Q26 from about 3% in 2025, with little in-housing. The main risk is digital-native independents winning accounts under $200m. Publicis is least exposed, while WPP and Omnicom are more exposed. GIR upgrades Stagwell to Buy with a $13 target (54% upside) and initiates Havas at Neutral with a €19 target (8% upside).

Outdoor advertising: global out-of-home trends are favourable. JCDecaux is best positioned. GS is slightly ahead of consensus on JCDecaux 3Q26 organic growth and in line on Stroeer revenue and EBITDA.
Auto1 3Q pre-close missed: units sold about 4% below consensus and adjusted EBITDA about 10% below. GS cuts 2026/27 EBITDA forecasts by c.4%/6%, keeps Buy and cuts the target to €32 from €37.

US trading: NDX hit a new all-time high, but rates backing up to pre-NFP levels kept risk appetite limited. The S&P is down seven straight weeks per the desk. Semis saw demand on MU earnings and NVDA buyback increases. Flow is spotty, with minimal willingness to chase despite light positioning.

GS Prime data: fundamental L/S managers were down 0.3% on the week and finished September down 0.6%, up 12.7% YTD. Systematic L/S were up 1.0% on the week, up 3.5% in September and 20.8% YTD. Europe was the most net bought region and EM Asia the most net sold. Info Tech, Communication Services and Consumer Discretionary were most net sold.
